slices.focus: Winter term results validate early-flagged apprentice improvements; forms standardized across all sections
slices.summary: Winter term outcomes show the early-flagged apprentice group stabilized rather than drifted, with better attendance and fewer repeat ladder and lockout-tagout write-ups. Based on this evidence, the training committee gives Derek real authority to standardize his check-in forms and skills sign-offs across all sections, transforming his personal pilot into the shared minimum. He wrestles with how to present this as a shared minimum rather than a personal victory, deciding to split the check-in form from the skills sign-offs, roll them out in stages, and let the evidence from the early-flagged group lead the conversation.
open_loops: Drafting a clean version of the shared minimum check-in form
Creating a separate skills sign-off document
Staggering rollout: form first, sign-offs second
Identifying non-negotiable core measures vs. flexible details
Handing off repeatable pieces so the system survives without him
decisions: Because the winter numbers held up, Derek was given authority to standardize first-year retention and safety tracking ac
The successful winter numbers eased Derek's fear that the added structure would become paperwork without real retention
